key_insight: DynaWeb adapts model-based reinforcement learning to web agents by learning a compact world model of the web so agents can train via simulated interactions, greatly reducing the need for costly and risky live-web exploration.
problem_solved: Training autonomous web agents on the live internet is inefficient, expensive, and unsafe; interacting with real web environments at scale prevents practical RL-driven agent development.
method: Learn an action-conditioned world model of web state transitions (e.g., DOM/API/response dynamics) from limited real interactions and logs.
Use the learned model to generate imagined rollouts for policy learning and planning, interleaving simulated training with occasional real rollouts for grounding.
Mitigate model bias via uncertainty-aware rollouts (ensembles or confidence gating) and selective real-environment fine-tuning.
impact: Enables sample-efficient, safer, and cheaper training of web-capable agents (including LLM-based assistants), accelerating development and deployment of autonomous web automation and assistance.

paper_title: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
